clue.text: Minor setback involving this classical trophy

parts.note: hic is Latin, the classical language, for 'this'
a cup is a sporting trophy

explanation.surface: A small reverse in a contest that put an ancient trophy at stake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Classical' points to Latin: HIC is Latin for 'this'. 'Involving' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: A hiccup is colloquially a small, temporary difficulty or setback.

clue.text: Unfavourable current state after car's overturned

indicators.note: after means the current and state come after the overturned car in the answer
overturned means the car's name is turned upside down, read bottom to top in this down clue

parts.note: the Mini is a classic British small car
I is the symbol for electric current
CAL is an abbreviation for California, a US state

explanation.surface: A grim political situation follows a car crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' reads the small car upward in this down entry, and 'after' puts the current and the state behind it. CAL is the postal-style short form for California.
explanation.definitionFit: Inimical means hostile or harmful, so a direct synonym of unfavourable.

clue.text: Supporting prisoner, attract scorn

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece supporting another sits beneath it, so tempt goes under the prisoner

parts.note: a con is slang for a convict
to tempt is to attract or entice

explanation.surface: Someone who stands up for a jailbird and draws derision.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'supporting' means placed below: TEMPT holds up CON.
explanation.definitionFit: Contempt and scorn are synonyms for a feeling that something is worthless.

clue.text: Plant from spot mostly occupied by sea eagle

indicators.note: occupied by means the sea eagle moves into the shortened spot
mostly means the last letter of the spot word is dropped

parts.note: a pimple is a spot on the skin
the erne is the white-tailed sea eagle, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A flower grows on a patch where a coastal raptor has settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' drops the spot's last letter, and 'occupied by' sets the eagle inside it. The answer is a wild flower, not a seaside plant, despite the coastal picture.
explanation.definitionFit: The scarlet pimpernel is a small wild flower of the primrose family.

clue.text: Goods recently purchased for giving away

definitions.meaning: the things bought on a trip to the shops
informing on someone to the authorities, British slang 'shop'

explanation.surface: Bought items to be donated.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopping means purchases, and in British slang to shop someone is to betray them to police.

clue.text: Starker-sounding lie once over this battleground auxiliary

indicators.note: over in a down clue places the lie above the second part

parts.note: a stretcher is an old slang term for a lie or exaggeration

indicators.note: sounding means the word for starker is said aloud to give a word spelt differently

parts.note: starker, more naked, means barer

explanation.surface: A grimmer falsehood told about a wartime helper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starker-sounding' means a word for starker said aloud, giving a different spelling; 'over' stacks the old fib on top. 'This' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretcher-bearer carries the wounded, an auxiliary role on a battlefield.

clue.text: Canon found page one missing from old recipe

indicators.note: missing from means the one is removed from the old recipe word

parts.note: receipt is an archaic word for a recipe
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A clergyman discovers a page lost from an antique cookbook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Canon' looks like a cleric, but it means a rule. RECEIPT without I is RECEPT.
explanation.definitionFit: A canon is a rule or principle, and a precept is a rule of conduct.

clue.text: Nark is angry about direction to slow down

indicators.note: about means the angry word goes round the musical direction

parts.note: irate means angry
rit., short for ritardando, is a musical direction to slow down

explanation.surface: An informer is furious at being told to ease off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nark' looks like the British slang noun for a police informer, but here it is the verb meaning to annoy. 'About' wraps the angry word round the musical direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To nark is British slang for to annoy, a synonym of irritate.

clue.text: Oliver installing new head — good for plant

indicators.note: installing a new head means the first letter is replaced

parts.note: Oliver Cromwell, Lord Protector of England

explanation.surface: A gardener named Oliver gets a fresh top, which is good for his flowers.
explanation.walkthrough: CROMWELL's head, C, is replaced by G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gromwell is a plant of the borage family with hard seeds.

clue.text: Inapt term actor used to cover errant son

indicators.note: used to cover means the actor goes round the scrambled son

parts.note: a mimer is an actor who performs in mime

indicators.note: errant means wandering astray, so the letters of son go astray

explanation.surface: A performer shields his wayward boy from a poor description.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Errant' scrambles the son, and 'used to cover' wraps the actor round the result. A mimer is a mime artist.
explanation.definitionFit: A misnomer is a wrong or unsuitable name, an inapt term.

clue.text: By trap in stream, study queer fish

parts.note: a weir can be a fence set in a stream to trap fish
to do a subject is to study it

explanation.surface: Beside a river barrier, one examines an odd fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By' is a link word. A queer fish is an old idiom for an odd person.
explanation.definitionFit: A queer fish is an eccentric person, exactly what weirdo means.

clue.text: Ring for help after shipwreck

parts.note: reads like phoning for assistance after a disaster at sea, but the ring is a buoyant hoop thrown to someone in the water

explanation.definitionFit: A buoyant ring thrown to people in the water to keep them afloat after a sinking.

clue.text: Confer after live point-to-point?

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
read as compass point S, the word to, then compass point W
read as compass point S, the word to, then compass point W
read as compass point S, the word to, then compass point W

explanation.surface: Giving out the prizes after a cross-country horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur steeplechase; split it as S (south) TO W (west). 'After' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To bestow is to confer or give as an honour.

clue.text: Inclination one has to write books after tea

indicators.note: after means the books come after the tea

parts.note: to pen is to write
cha is British slang for tea
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible

explanation.surface: A writer's urge to get the books done once tea is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One has' is a link phrase, and 'after' puts the New Testament books behind the tea. Cha is old British slang for tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A penchant is a liking or strong inclination for something.

clue.text: Go on miles circulating coinage

indicators.note: circulating means the letters move round into a new order

explanation.surface: Money going round over long distances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coinage' suggests money, which 'circulating' encourages, but it means a newly coined word.
explanation.definitionFit: A neologism is a newly invented word, a verbal coinage.

clue.text: Foolish person possibly felt less hot

indicators.note: less means the hot letter is taken away

parts.note: felt is an example of a cloth, hence 'possibly'
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An idiot who may have felt less heated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' looks like a verb but is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A clot is British slang for a stupid person.

clue.text: Butterfly has no date with old soldier

parts.note: the comma is a British butterfly with a comma-shaped mark
n.d. is the bibliographic abbreviation for no date

explanation.surface: An insect with no fixed day joins a veteran.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Has' and 'with' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A commando is a soldier trained for raids.

clue.text: Fine fruit invaded by a growth made by wasp

indicators.note: invaded by means the a gets inside the fine fruit

parts.note: OK means fine or all right
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Good produce attacked by a wasp-made growth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invaded by' sends the letter A into the word for fine, before the fruit. Oak apples are galls, swellings caused by wasp larvae.
explanation.definitionFit: An oak apple is a gall formed on oak trees by gall wasp larvae.

clue.text: Authentic-sounding music for dance

indicators.note: sounding means the word for authentic is said aloud

parts.note: real means authentic or genuine

explanation.surface: Genuine-sounding tunes to dance to.
explanation.definitionFit: A reel is a lively Scottish dance and the tune played for it.

clue.text: Royal person developing firearm

parts.note: an evolver is one who evolves or develops

explanation.surface: A member of the royal family designing a gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolver is a handgun with a rotating cylinder, a type of firearm.

clue.text: Omission of words as priest's sealing lips

indicators.note: sealing means the priest's name closes round the lips

parts.note: Eli was the priest in the Old Testament who raised Samuel

explanation.surface: A priest keeping his mouth shut leaves words unsaid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As' is a link word; 'sealing' has the priest's name close round the mouth. Eli is the Old Testament priest who brought up Samuel.
explanation.definitionFit: An ellipsis is the leaving out of words from a sentence, often marked by dots.

clue.text: Circle surrounding head's untidy room in Bow, say?

indicators.note: Bow is in London's East End, where Cockneys drop the h, so the phrase is said aloud Cockney style

parts.note: a glory hole is a cluttered room or cupboard, said with the h dropped

explanation.surface: A halo round someone's head in a messy East End room.
explanation.walkthrough: A glory hole is an untidy storeroom; a Cockney from Bow says GLORY 'OLE, which sounds like the answer. The 's is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A gloriole is a halo or aureole, a ring of light round a head.

clue.text: Ape and gazelle crossing stream

indicators.note: crossing means the gazelle stretches across the stream

parts.note: the goa is a Tibetan gazelle
a rill is a small stream

explanation.surface: A primate and an antelope fording a brook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossing' has the gazelle span the stream; 'and' is a link word. The goa is a little-known Tibetan gazelle.
explanation.definitionFit: A gorilla is the largest ape.

clue.text: After a mile, tidal wave becomes weak

indicators.note: after means the tidal wave comes after the mile

parts.note: M is the abbreviation for a mile
an eagre is a tidal bore in a river

explanation.surface: A tidal surge loses its force after a mile.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becomes' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or feeble, so weak.

clue.text: Inexpensive English periodical entertaining small number

indicators.note: entertaining means holding the small number inside

parts.note: a comic is a periodical magazine
no. is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A cheap English magazine with a small circulation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Entertaining' has the periodical hold the small number. A comic is a children's magazine of strips.
explanation.definitionFit: Economic can mean cheap or giving good value, as in an economic price.

clue.text: Language inappropriate in Alpine resort

indicators.note: inappropriate means the letters are put in the wrong order
resort is read as re-sort, sorting the letters again

explanation.surface: Unsuitable speech at a ski village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Resort' looks like a holiday place but reads as re-sort. 'In' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nepali is the official language of Nepal.

clue.text: Lay out more money to mount further siege

definitions.meaning: to put money back into investments
to invest is an old sense of besieging, so to besiege again

explanation.surface: Spend more cash on a renewed siege.
explanation.definitionFit: To reinvest is to put more money in, and invest also means to lay siege.

clue.text: One makes connections: in exchange for income

definitions.text: One makes connections: in exchange for income

parts.words: One makes connections: in exchange for income
parts.note: reads like a trader or deal-maker, but describes someone paid to connect calls at a telephone exchange

explanation.definitionFit: A switchboard worker at a telephone exchange who connects callers in return for wages.

clue.text: Gloomy inspector consuming duck

indicators.note: consuming means the inspector swallows the duck

parts.note: Inspector Morse is the TV detective
a duck is a zero score in cricket, O

explanation.surface: A downbeat detective eating poultry.
explanation.walkthrough: Inspector Morse is a famously gloomy fictional detective, which helps the surface. O goes inside MORSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Morose means sullen and gloomy.
